newsitem.title: UK: UK's Labour leader expects March election.
newsitem.headline: UK's Labour leader expects March election.

text.p: The deputy leader of Britain's opposition Labour Party said on Sunday he expected Prime Minister John Major to call an election in March instead of hanging on to power until the last possible moment in May.
"I think what we have to do is put the election machine on a (war) footing for March 20," Labour deputy leader John Prescott said in a BBC television interview.
Major, trailing Labour in the polls, has already lost his overall majority in parliament through deaths and defections.
His ruling party would slip into a minority if, as expected, it loses a by-election in the Wirral seat formerly held by Conservative MP Barry Porter, who died last November.

Although Major can hold on to power even without an overall majority thanks to the support of small parties such as the nine-strong Ulster Unionists, he has delayed setting the Wirral by-election date until the last minute.

Ruling party sources said last week they would announce the by-election date, expected to be February 27, on Monday. Some commentators say Major, keen to avoid a humiliating by-election trouncing and believing he has better chances of reversing Labour's poll lead in a full-blown campaign, will call it off at the last minute and call a national election instead.
Prescott, interviewed by David Frost, agreed, saying: "I don't trust them, I don't believe what Tories say any more...

"I think just as they get near that election date in the Wirral they'll call it off, announce a general election and therefore they won't have that indictment on them which I think will come on February 27 if they allow it to take place." Polls give Labour a lead of around 20 points over the Conservatives, who have now held power for an unbroken 18 years.
Major's attempts to unite his party and fight back have consistently run into trouble, usually over Europe.

In a new blow on Sunday, a Conservative parliamentarian who was sacked as the party's candidate after calling Major "a ventriloquist's dummy" said he was prepared to oppose the ruling party at the election if they did not relent and take him back.

Sir George Gardiner, a so-called Eurosceptic Conservative who opposes closer links with Europe, was told on Thursday he was no longer the candidate for the southern English seat of Reigate he has represented in parliament for 23 years.

On Sunday he renewed his attacks on Major, saying the prime minister was "so washed up we could see he was very near to throwing in the towel", and pledged to stand as a "genuine Conservative" at the election whether he was reinstated as official candidate or not.
The head of the body representing rank-and-file Conservative MPs, Sir Marcus Fox, appealed to Gardiner to reconsider, saying he would do "considerable damage to his own colleagues".
The row merely underlined deep Conservative splits over moves towards greater European integration.

That view was underlined on Sunday by reports that senior Conservatives, under pressure from those who want a tougher line on Europe, have decided to allow official candidates to make campaign commitments which go beyond government policy.
